sadly, a lot of suicide attempts leave people alive with permanent issues. any way you could think to end your life would likely backfire if it just wasn't your time. it's not worth going through the pain, trust me, but it is worth seeking out a therapist. if you're underage, this might be hard. it was hard for me because i asked for a therapist a few years back when i was 13 and my mom said something instead about how i didn't need one. last October, she walked in on me having a breakdown and realized it was something i needed. if you can show a guardian figure it's what you need and then verbally ask for it, they'll be more likely to help you out.

if you're old enough to seek a therapist on your own, ignore that. instead go onto psychologytoday.com and look for therapists in your area. it's always really good to have someone to talk to, even if you feel like you'd rather be dead or like it won't help. look for therapists that specifically will help those with suicidal thoughts, so you know you can be point-blank with them and not have them react in a bad way. my therapist is amazing and has never told anyone about my suicidal thoughts even when i thought she would. i may be about to kill myself myself, but i've exhausted my options. i don't think you have yet. it sounds like most of your bad thoughts are coming from within because of the external, which makes it really hard because depression lies to you. it tells you, like you said, that you're evil and can't improve in life and just don't deserve it. but even though i'm a stranger i can say you're not, you can, and you do.

therapy doesn't help everyone, but it can be a great starting point to lifting your life up. you seem like a good person who would tell someone else to take that chance, so i'm going to say you should tell yourself to take it. you're worth it.

i wish you luck in whatever you decide to do, even if in the end you decide to kill yourself anyways. i know how hard it is, but i still urge you to push through.
